Interchanged Project 58317: Data Center
Development Policy Change Proposal
Prepared For: Interchanged Project 58317 Stakeholders and Regulatory Review Boards
Subject: Comprehensive Community Protection Mandates for Infrastructure Expansion

As community advocates and stakeholders reviewing Interchanged Project 58317, we submit
this formal document to establish non-negotiable boundaries regarding regional data center
development. While technological infrastructure expands, it must not be prioritized over the
financial stability of working-class families, local food security, natural habitats, and
neighborhood integrity. This document outlines the protective policies that must be integrated
into Project 58317 before any development is authorized.

1. Protection of Local Utility Bills (Electricity and
Water)
Data center facilities demand unprecedented amounts of electrical power and water, which
threatens the stability and affordability of municipal resources.
   ●​ The Threat: When massive corporate facilities monopolize the public grid, utility providers
      frequently pass infrastructure upgrade costs on to local residents, artificially inflating
      monthly utility bills. Furthermore, traditional cooling methods evaporate millions of gallons
      of fresh water daily. Rich corporations must not shift their operational costs onto poor and
      working-class families who work hard for every dollar.
   ●​ Policy Mandate: Developers must be legally required to build or invest in independent,
      off-grid renewable energy sources (such as dedicated solar or wind installations). They
      must not draw from the public residential grid. Furthermore, facilities must implement
      closed-loop, waterless cooling systems or utilize recycled gray water to ensure local
      drinking water supplies remain entirely unaffected.

2. Halting the Destruction of Productive Farmland
The rapid rezoning of agricultural land for industrial tech campuses permanently damages
regional food security.
  ●​ The Threat: Selling off productive farmland permanently destroys fertile topsoil and strips
      communities of the space required to grow crops. Our farmlands are vital resources for
      regional sustenance and must be preserved rather than liquidated for corporate profits.
  ●​ Policy Mandate: A strict moratorium must be placed on converting active agricultural
      zones into industrial data center facilities. Regulatory frameworks should restrict
      development exclusively to brownfield sites, abandoned industrial properties, or
      underutilized commercial zones.

3. Preserving Wildlife and Natural Ecosystems
 Large-scale industrial construction disrupts local ecosystems and drives native species from
their natural environments.
  ●​ The Threat: Clear-cutting land fragments native habitats, destroying the homes of local
       wildlife. This ecological displacement forces wild animals out of their natural habitats and
       directly into residential neighborhoods, creating safety hazards for families and animals
       alike.
  ●​ Policy Mandate: Developers must implement strict wildlife corridors and leave
       substantial portions of natural terrain completely untouched. Comprehensive
       environmental impact assessments must be completed—and fully approved by the local
       community—before any site construction is permitted.

4. Preventing Economic Displacement and
Gentrification
High-capital tech projects frequently distort local real estate markets, pricing out long-term
homeowners and tenants.
  ●​ The Threat: Wealthy corporations and industrial developers use financial leverage to
      drive up property valuations and taxes. This systematically pushes hard-working,
      low-income, and working-class families out of the homes they have labored for decades
      to secure and maintain.
  ●​ Policy Mandate: Project 58317 must build protective tax-stabilization barriers for existing
      residential zones. Corporate interests must be blocked from using aggressive buyout
      tactics or eminent domain to clear out local neighborhoods. Community-led zoning boards
      must retain final veto power over any proposed development project.

Conclusion: Infrastructure growth under Interchanged Project 58317 must not come at the
expense of human lives, community resources, or the natural environment. We demand that
these strict, protective regulations be formally adopted to ensure local residents and resources
are fully protected.
